_what: This repo's proof-tested guards. Read by Forge/guards/run-guards.py. The `discover` command enumerates every `audit:*` npm script, so --coverage reports the TRUE gap rather than the size of this hand-written list — which is the whole point, and the defect the registry exists to prevent.

guards.what: static secret + injection scan across src, backend, scripts, config, tests, public and root config
guards.why: the reference implementation for control corpora. The PREVIOUS hardcoded-secret rule sat green in test:compliance while blind to every real credential — it demanded 20+ chars (the leaked password was 14), excluded punctuation, never read .php or .xml, and skipped any line containing 'test'. It now self-tests against scripts/fixtures/sast-secret-corpus.txt and REFUSES to scan if the corpus fails.
guards.proof_note: the corpus check is IN the run — a corpus failure aborts the scan, so running it is proving it. Split into a distinct --self-test if that coupling ever loosens.

guards.what: vocabulary sync between the canonical term list and its consumers
guards.why: verify-vocabulary-sync.ts carries fixture-based cases; registered so the fixtures are exercised on a schedule.
guards.unproven_reason: references fixtures but exposes no --self-test entry point; needs a paired must-catch/must-ignore case before it can be called proven.
